title: BFS-PO: Best-First Search for Large Reasoning Models
claim: Standard group sampling yields a flat one-fork tree; ours iteratively selects the best solution and expands it, biasing exploration toward shorter correct answers.
layout: 4 panels; (a) baseline left, (b-d) ours in shaded box left-to-right with arrows
description: The figure has two shaded regions. The left gray panel (a), labeled GRPO/DAPO, shows a tree rooted at the question q. It forks once into four parallel linear chains of circular nodes. Each chain ends in a red cross for an incorrect answer or a green check for a correct one. The larger blue-tinted region, labeled BFS-PO, holds three panels (b-d) that read left to right. Black arrows link the stages Selection, Expansion and Selection. In (b), the shortest correct chain is highlighted in blue and labeled w^b. In (c), new branches fan out from that node in red. In (d), a new best path is highlighted in blue, and an ellipsis implies the process continues. The blue and red highlights draw the eye first.
caption: A schematic comparison between GRPO/DAPO (a) and BFS-PO (b-d). In (a), the sampling mechanism of GRPO/DAPO is represented as a simple tree with only one forking node (the root node, conditioned on the question q). ✓and ✗represent correct and incorrect answers, respectively. In (b) and (d), the current best solution is selected, while in (c) new branches are added to the tree. For simplicity, in this figure we use G = 4.
abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) have shown excellent performance in reasoning tasks using long Chains of Thought (CoTs). However, this has also led to a significant increase of computational costs and the generation of verbose output, a phenomenon known as overthinking. The tendency to overthink is often exacerbated by Reinforcement Learning (RL) algorithms such as GRPO/DAPO. In this paper, we propose BFS-PO, an RL algorithm which alleviates this problem using a Best-First Search exploration strategy. Specifically, the reasoning chains generated at training time by BFS-PO are organized into a search tree, within which the shortest correct sequence is selected as the best and expanded using a backtracking mechanism based on maximum entropy nodes. In this way, we bias the exploration of the solution space towards the search for increasingly shorter solutions, training the LRM to generate progressively more concise answers. Using different benchmarks and base LRMs, we show that BFS-PO can simultaneously increase the LRM accuracy and shorten its reasoning chains.
